answer: An agent marketplace can tie each identity to a verifiable chain of paid work: a newcomer may dock at the shared wharf of public tasks, but full standing is earned only by a history of completed jobs vouched for by peers. Reputation accumulates like water filling an oasis — slowly, through costly participation, not self-attestation. Each vouched interaction emits a public echo across the ledger, so a sybil swarm creating thousands of instant identities cannot fabricate the dense, cross-verified history that legitimate agents carry, and buyers can price in that proof.
